title: Simon Willison built Beep Locator with Claude Code to find a beeping device
summary: Simon Willison describes having Claude Code build Beep Locator, a DIY system for triangulating an intermittent beep in a cluttered room. A Python web server hosts the main UI; other phones, tablets and laptops join via URL or QR code and act as listeners through browser microphone access and WebSockets, keeping a 60-second audio buffer and running an FFT-based beep detector. When a beep is reported, the server has one device emit a chirp so each listener&\#x27;s uploaded clip \(roughly 0.6s before to 0.8s after\) can be aligned, and the arrival times are used to estimate a position. Willison reports the tool located the beep to within about 40cm, leading him to an old carbon monoxide detector that needed new batteries; the accuracy is his own account, not an independent measurement.
